text:
Brandon Montour is playing like a man who's been handed the keys. He's averaging 24:16 a night, up to about 25 over his last ten games, and he has 15 points in 19 games. That's already about half of last season's 32 in 64.

Our numbers like the effort and doubt the pace. He scores 1.95 points per 60, above his likely range of 1.19 to 1.75. The main reason is that Seattle has scored 6.1 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, the kind of luck that tends to fade. His own scoring is fine: 3 goals on 2.4 expected.

There's plenty to like. He's among the most explosive skaters in the league by NHL EDGE bursts over 20 mph (96th percentile), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a setup man last season, 83rd percentile in primary shot assists among defensemen, joining the rush far more than most. Evolving-Hockey also found last season that his chances outran his results with weak teammates around him. This year the bounces have swung the other way. Our middle projection is 54 points, still a strong year for a Stanley Cup winner at 32.
headline: Montour's point pace is outrunning his process
